title: Do You Have Enemies?
body:
As Christians, we have enemies, both physical and spiritual. Even when things are going well for us, and we are experiencing the mighty blessings of God, Satan is there, somewhere in the background, walking about "seeking whom he may devour".
-(1 Peter5:8)

Sometimes he uses people. "For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, that they are the enemies of the cross of Christ", (Philippians 3:18)

Psalm 58 is one of many imprecatory Psalms, and reminds us we can, and should, deal with the enemy. Even in the good times.

Prepare for the Enemy (v1-5)

Expect the enemy to be:

Unrighteous and Unjust (v1)

Heartless and Violent (v2)

Wicked from the womb (v3)

Speaking lies (v3)

Poisonous, dangerous, and out of control (v4-5)

Pray Against the Enemy (v6-8)

Pray their Power will be Disabled (v6)

Pray their Plans will be Disappointed (v7)

Pray their Purpose will be Destroyed (v8)

Perceive the Ultimate Destruction of the Enemy (v9-11)

Their destruction comes quickly and surely. (v9)

Their destruction comes with God's wrath. (v9)

Their destruction comes with God's vengeance. (v10)

Their destruction comes with God's righteous judgement. (v11)

How to destroy an enemy:
"Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head. Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good." (Romans 12:20-21)

If you are living as an enemy of God, God's people desire you to be saved from the wrath and judgement that is sure to come.

That is also God's desire for you!

"Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life." (Romans 5:9-10)

title: Are You an Enemy of God?
body:
In the midst of writing about his rejoicing and joy concerning the type of church the Thessalonians had become, the Apostle Paul turned his thoughts to the enemies of the church in 1 Thessalonians 2:15-16.

#1. They Fight the Power of God (v15)
          They killed the Lord Jesus
          They killed the prophets
          They persecuted the apostles

Stephen spoke to them this way in Acts 7:51-52:  "Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost:  as your fathers did, so do ye.  Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and they have slain them which shewed before of the coming of the Just One; of whom you have been now the betrayers and murderers:"  Six verses later they stoned him to death.

Lost people today are not just fighting the people of God, but they are fighting the very Power of God those people represent! Power that is mighty to save!
Are you fighting God's power? "ye do always resist the Holy Ghost"

#2. They Forbid the Word of God (v16a)
         "that they might be saved"

"But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name." (John 20:31)

Most lost folks today are not forbidding the Word of God from being preached, but they all ARE forbidding the Word of God from taking root in their heart so that they might be saved.

Are you forbidding God's Word to have its effectual work in your life?

#3. They Fill Up Their Sin Against God (v16b)
           "to fill up their sins alway"

As Jesus spoke to the Jews, "Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do..." John 8:44.

In Genesis 15:16 God noted to Abraham that "the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full".  But eventually their iniquity (sin) caught up with them.
God is "not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance." (2 Peter 3:9)

“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”  (1 John 1:9)

Are you filling up your sin against God?

#4 They Face the Wrath of God (v16c)
        "for the wrath is come upon them to the uttermost"

In Ephesians 5 Paul gives a long list of common sins that people try to get away with.  Then he writes in verse 6 "Let no man deceive you with vain words: for because of these things cometh the wrath of God upon the children of disobedience."

Are you facing the wrath of God?

You don't have to face God's wrath.  You can be saved and forgiven!  It all comes down to faith and belief.

"He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life:  and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him." (John 3:36)

None of us should be God's enemy!

Please, do NOT:
     Fight the Power of God
     Forbid the Word of God
     Fill Up Sin Against God
     Face the Wrath of God
